# Otto — OLT support agent

## Escalation notifications

Both settings are optional because the destination is undecided (`KU-14`).
Unset, the api starts normally, records escalations at
`no_destination_configured`, notifies nobody and logs one
`escalation.no_destination` warning at startup. In the chart,
`api.escalationWebhookSecretName` names a Secret with the keys `url` and,
optionally, `token`. The records live in the `escalations` collection, so a
record and its place in the retry schedule survive a restart. A record whose
process died mid-send is claimed again by the next process after 10 minutes, so
the destination may receive it twice.

# Human access to the support agent's GCP projects

Repository: `re-cinq/Otto`, private. The file that declares who may read a
customer's conversation is `infra/terraform/access/main.tf`; this page explains
it. Cite both at one commit.

The api's logs land in Cloud Logging, so whoever can read the project's logs can
read what a customer typed. This page and the terraform root hold work email
addresses, role names and a one-line reason per person, and nothing else.

Escalation is a stated product requirement, not a fallback. Kristian's target and anti-target are both explicit: an insurance robot that took too long to admit it needed to transfer him, versus a tax-authority chat that gave up quickly and was a better experience for it - and the intended destination is a phone call, with OLT contacting the customer as soon as the agent can't answer. `MongoSessionStore`, so a conversation outlives both its socket and the process,

collection. Every model turn also leaves one row in `auditEntries`, kept 365
days: the session and user ids, when and how long, the model and tool names, the
token counts and how the turn ended, never what anyone wrote. A provider
failover adds a row of its own, with no session or user: the two provider types,
the error code and how long the failed call ran. A tool call that
